info.title: Afisharr
info.description: Plex collections, posters, and overlay manager.

post.summary: Signs in with a username and a password.
post.description:
The limiter is consulted before the hash and recorded after it, and only on
failure: a limit that counted successes would lock out the operator signing
in from a fourth device (PRD §21.4.3).

That ordering is what makes the failure count honest, and it is also why the
limiter cannot be the only thing standing in front of the hash: an attempt
that has not finished has not failed, so a burst arriving inside one instant
passes the check together and nothing here has counted any of it yet. The
bound that holds for a burst is a bound on the work itself —
`accounts::verify` admits a fixed number of Argon2id operations at a time,
so extra requests wait for a permit instead of each allocating 64 MiB.

400.description: The request body was not readable

403.description: Setup has not been completed on this instance

parameters.description: The path inside the root. Empty means the root itself.

get.summary: Reports that the instance is up.
get.description:
The 429 is declared because the group carries a rate limit, and a layer
answering on a route's behalf must be in that route's own annotations: the
generated client is built from them and nothing else, so an undeclared answer
is one the interface simply does not handle (§24.5).

403.description: That account does not administer this instance, or setup has not been completed

post.summary: Issues a key and returns its plaintext, once.

403.description: That account does not administer this instance, or setup has not been completed

delete.summary: Revokes one key. It is refused on its next use.

403.description: That account does not administer this instance, or setup has not been completed

404.description: No such key, or it was already revoked

post.description:
Everything PRD §21.4.2 asks for happens here and happens together, in one
transaction: the current password is re-verified, the new hash is written,
every session for the account is revoked, and a replacement is inserted for
the browser that asked. Rotation is not decoration — a session identifier
that survives a password change survives the theft the change was made to
end — and a rotation split across separate commits has a window in which
exactly that is true.

401.description: The current password was not accepted

403.description: Setup has not been completed on this instance

409.description: That account has no password to change, or another change reached it first

403.description: Setup has not been completed on this instance

delete.summary: Revokes one of the signed-in account's sessions.

403.description: Setup has not been completed on this instance

404.description: No such session on this account

post.description:
Reachable only behind the claim gate, and only while no administrator
exists. The moment this page is reachable on an instance that may face the
internet it is an unauthenticated grant of administrator, which is why the
gate arrives with it rather than eleven phases later (D-045).

400.description: The username or password was refused

403.description: The claim on this wizard has expired

get.summary: Reports what the claim page needs, without a claim.
get.description:
`/api/setup/status` sits behind the claim gate, so an unclaimed browser can
never read it — which is correct for the derived step and useless for the
page that has to be drawn *before* a claim exists. Left to guess, the
interface fabricates: a hard-coded `recoveryAvailable: false` hides the
recovery form from the operator whose token has died with a restart, and a
hard-coded `tokenLive: true` offers a token field on an instance that has
no live token to accept.

Neither fact is a disclosure. "An administrator exists" is already the
difference between `/api/setup/recover` accepting credentials and refusing
them, and "a token is live" is already the difference between a claim
attempt being refused and being possible at all.

post.summary: Takes the wizard for this browser, on the strength of the console token.

200.description: The wizard is now held by this browser

400.description: The request body was not readable

post.description:
Four things happen together and none is optional (PRD §19.6.1):
`instance.setup_completed_at` is written, the `setup:claim` lease is
deleted, the in-memory token is cleared, and the cookie is expired. From
then on the banner prints nothing on restart and these endpoints answer 404.

All four are irreversible, which is why the prerequisite is checked first.

403.description: The claim on this wizard has expired

409.description: Another browser holds the wizard, or no administrator exists yet

post.summary: Takes the wizard on administrator credentials, once an account exists.
post.description:
The recovery path (PRD §19.6.1): the token dies with the process, the
account does not, so an interrupted setup survives a restart.

200.description: The wizard is now held by this browser

400.description: The request body was not readable

get.summary: Reports the step this instance resumes at.
get.description:
The step is computed here and never accepted from the caller. A step index
in a query string, a cookie, or a client-held draft would let a caller name
the step they would like to be on, which on the claim step means naming
step 2 (D-046, `I-UX-10`). There is no parameter on this route to supply
one with.

403.description: The claim on this wizard has expired

get.description:
Requires authentication, like every other route on this surface — the
stream carries job progress and source health, which name the operator's
libraries and integrations.

The stream never replays. A client that reconnects has missed events and
knows it; the answer is to refetch the surfaces it feeds, which is what a
fresh page load does anyway (PRD §9). Building a replay buffer would make
two paths to the same state, and the one that is exercised less would be
the one that is wrong (P7).

200.description: The event stream, multiplexed by topic

403.description: That account does not administer this instance, or setup has not been completed

ApiKeyView.description:
A key as the list shows it.

No field here authenticates anything. The prefix tells two keys apart and
the digest is not in the shape at all, so an operator who screenshots this
page has leaked nothing.

createdAt.description: When it was issued, in epoch milliseconds.

id.description: The key's identifier, which is what revocation names.

lastUsedAt.description: When it was last accepted, in epoch milliseconds.

prefix.description: The first eight characters, for display.

revokedAt.description: When it was revoked, in epoch milliseconds.

ClaimGranted.description: A claim now held by this browser.

expiresAt.description: When the hold lapses if nothing renews it, in epoch milliseconds.

ClaimRequest.description: The token an operator copies off the console.

token.description: The three four-character segments, as printed.

ClaimStatus.description:
The two facts the claim page renders, and whether it already holds a claim.

Deliberately not the derived step and deliberately not `Evidence`: this route
is outside the claim gate, so it says the least that lets step one draw
itself and nothing about how far setup has got (D-046).

claimHeld.description: Whether this browser already holds the wizard.

ordinal.description:
The claim step's position in the journey, one-based, for display only.

Carried rather than assumed, for the same reason `/api/setup/status`
carries it: the shape of the journey is the server's to state, and a
number written into a page is a number that goes stale in silence.

recoveryAvailable.description:
Whether an administrator account exists, which decides whether the claim
page offers the recovery affordance (PRD §7.14).

tokenLive.description:
Whether a token is live to be entered at all.

False fifteen minutes after a start with no restart, which is what turns
the page's message from "enter the token" into "restart the container
and read the console".

username.description: The name the account will sign in with.

entries.description: The entries, directories first and then by name.

EntryView.description: One entry in a browsed directory.

isDirectory.description: Whether it can be descended into.

path.description:
The path relative to the root, which is what a caller asks for next.

Relative and never absolute: an absolute path would tell a caller where
the root lives, which is the one thing the refusal message is careful
not to disclose.

sizeBytes.description: Size in bytes, for a file.

ErrorCode.description:
What kind of failure this is.

A closed enum with an exhaustive status mapping, so the generated client
narrows on a value it knows rather than on a number. Adding a variant is a
contract change that shows up in the regenerated client, which is the
point: a new failure mode the interface has never heard of should not be
able to arrive silently as a 500.

Health.description:
What the health route reports.

Deliberately thin. A container orchestrator asks this before anyone has
signed in, so it must not name libraries, integrations, or anything else
that describes the operator's setup — this is the one route with no
credential in front of it (`I-SEC-8` excepts it by name).

setupCompleted.description:
Whether first-run setup has finished.

The one fact beyond liveness, and it is already observable from outside:
an unclaimed instance answers every other route with `setupRequired`.
Reporting it here lets the interface route to the claim page on its
first load instead of learning it from a refusal.

status.description: Always `ok` when this route answers at all.

allOf.description: The key as the list will show it from now on.

secret.description: The plaintext. Shown once; this instance cannot produce it again.

IssuedKey.description: A key at the one moment its plaintext exists.

Mismatch.description:
What was expected against what arrived.

Carried as a pair rather than folded into the message, because the
interface renders them as two labelled values and a message it has to parse
is a message that stops being renderable the first time the wording changes.

expected.description: What the field should have held, in the operator's terms.

NewApiKey.description: What the operator names a new key.

name.description: A name the operator will recognise later.

currentPassword.description: The password in force now, re-entered.

sessionsRevoked.description:
How many other sessions were revoked.

Reported rather than silent: the point of revoking them is that the
operator knows the other devices are signed out.

authorizationUrl.description: Where to send the operator, for the OAuth variant.

code.description: The four-character code, for the PIN variant.

expiresAt.description: When plex.tv stops answering for this pin, in epoch milliseconds.

id.description: Afisharr's identifier for this attempt. The client polls this.

oneOf.description: plex.tv has not seen the operator finish. Poll again.
A token arrived and a session was created.

isAdmin.description:
Whether that account administers this instance.

Reported rather than assumed. A linked Plex account that is not an
administrator gets a session with `is_admin = false`, and a client
that recorded it as an administrator would route the operator into
admin-only pages that answer 403 (`I-UX-2`).

oneOf.description: The pin's window closed without a token.

PinState.description:
What one poll found.

Three states, and the client renders three different things. Folding
`expired` into `pending` would leave an operator watching a spinner for a
code that will never be accepted (P1).

Problem.description:
The body of every failed response on this surface.

The JSON pointer is what lets a form put the message beside the field that
caused it, rather than in a banner at the top that names nothing. It is
RFC 6901 — `/sources/2/kind`, not `sources[2].kind` — so the client can walk
the request body it already holds.

code.description: What kind of failure this is. The client narrows on this.

message.description: One sentence, in the operator's terms, naming what failed (PRD §8.4).

oneOf.description: The expected-versus-actual pair, when there is one.

pointer.description: An RFC 6901 pointer into the request body, when one field caused this.

retryAfterSeconds.description:
When the caller may try again, in seconds. Set on a rate-limited or
blocked answer, and matching the `Retry-After` header.

RecoverRequest.description: The administrator credentials that recover an interrupted setup.

RootView.description: One root the operator has allowed.

id.description:
The identifier the browser addresses it by.

The row's own key rather than the label: two roots of one purpose can
share a final directory name, so a label is allowed to collide and
addressing by it would make the second of them unreachable.

label.description: The operator's name for it, which is what a refusal reads out.

SessionView.description: One session, as the settings page lists it.

createdAt.description: When it was created, in epoch milliseconds.

id.description:
The digest, which is what revocation names.

Safe to show: it is the SHA-256 of a cookie value, and knowing it does
not let anyone present the value it came from.

ip.description: The address it was created from.

isCurrent.description: Whether this is the session making the request.

lastSeenAt.description: When it was last used, in epoch milliseconds.

revokedAt.description: When it was revoked, in epoch milliseconds.

userAgent.description: The user agent recorded when it was created.

SetupStatus.description: Where the wizard is, derived from what the database holds.

claimHeld.description: Whether this browser holds the claim.

ordinal.description: Its position in the journey, one-based, for display only.

recoveryAvailable.description:
Whether an administrator account exists, which decides whether the
claim page offers the recovery affordance (PRD §7.14).

tokenLive.description:
Whether a token is live to be entered at all.

False after fifteen minutes with no restart, which is what turns the
claim page's message from "enter the token" into "restart the container
and read the console".

displayName.description: The name to show, when it differs from the account name.

isAdmin.description: Whether the account holds administrator rights.

StartPin.description: What the interface asks for when it starts a Plex sign-in.

forwardUrl.description:
Where plex.tv returns the operator, for the OAuth variant.

It must be on this instance's configured `publicOrigin`. plex.tv
redirects to whatever this asks for, so a target anywhere else turns the
endpoint into a redirector wearing a legitimate `app.plex.tv/auth` URL,
and the operator who completes the sign-in lands on somebody else's
page.

oauth.description:
`pin` shows a four-character code; `oauth` sends the operator to
plex.tv's hosted sign-in.

StepView.description:
A step, as the generated client sees it.

A mirror of [`SetupStep`] rather than a `ToSchema` derive on the domain
type, so `afisharr-core` stays free of the HTTP surface's annotations
(§24.6.1). The `From` below is exhaustive, so a step added to the domain
fails to compile here rather than reaching the client as a string it cannot
narrow.
